narratives.Overview:
## AppSec remediation

- **Product:** Directive (`deftai/directive`)
- **Finding:** `hooks-authz-05`
- **Severity:** medium
- **Scan:** 2026-10-05 @ `d855dc0f784a24ed6d99cffd488a85f41d22431c`
- **Report:** [2026-10-05 AppSec report § directive / hooks-authz-05](https://github.com/deftai/appsec-scans/blob/3dd35fd7f6b54922c56759157c13c821b4374dec/reports/directive/2026-10-05/report.md#directive-hooks-authz-05)

### Impact

A write whose dest sits in an unharvested field (MCP `uri`, nested non-pathish dest) is allowed under active UAT and a live occupancy/write-fence that would deny the same tool once `path` is present. Inner `run_terminal_command`/`Bash` via `use_tool`/`CallMcpTool` never hits the Shell/UAT classifier.

### Remediation

Fail closed when the name is write-shaped (or an MCP/proxy wrapper whose inner name is write- or shell-shaped) and dest harvest is empty, matching ApplyPatch. Harvest MCP `uri`/`file` dests. After unwrap, re-run `isShellTool(effectiveName)` / `isDirectWriteTool(effectiveName)` so inner Grok shell cannot skip the Shell slice. Keep `relPathPosix === null` from silently allowing an active write fence.

Filed by the scheduled AppSec scan. Do not close until the control is in the default branch. The next weekly scan will comment here if this ID is still confirmed.

## In plain English
PreToolUse lets some write-shaped MCP/proxy calls skip the write fence when the dest path sits in fields we do not harvest (uri/file) or when harvest is empty. Inner shell via use_tool/CallMcpTool can also skip the Shell classifier. Prefer-A matches ApplyPatch: fail closed on empty harvest for write-shaped names, harvest uri/file, and after unwrap re-classify shell vs direct-write so the right slice runs.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. Harvest MCP uri/file (and keep existing pathish keys) in hookMutationTargetPaths / collectPathishFields.
2. Fail closed when effective name is write-shaped (or proxy wrapper whose inner is write- or shell-shaped) and dest harvest is empty — same class as ApplyPatch unclassified-body deny.
3. After effectiveHookToolName unwrap, re-run isShellTool(effectiveName) / isDirectWriteTool(effectiveName) (and isMcpWriteShaped) so inner Grok shell hits the Shell/UAT slice.
4. Keep relPathPosix === null from silently allowing an active write fence (deny under fence when path cannot be classified).
5. file_scope: packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts (+tests), packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts (+tests as needed), packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts (+tests), CHANGELOG.md.
6. Keep-outs: do not rewrite #3593 MCP write-shaped admission grammar wholesale; do not absorb unrelated authz classify Shell harvest (#4199); do not weaken ApplyPatch empty-body deny.

Reject (draft): harvest-only without empty-harvest fail-closed; fail-open docs-only; treating outer use_tool name as non-write forever without unwrap reclassify.

## In plain English
The proposed direction closes real gaps, but it needs two explicit rules before binding: unwrap the command arguments as well as the tool name, and convert supported file URIs into actual filesystem paths before checking the fence. A nonempty string is not proof that the destination has been understood.

Verification: pin-read via git show at 97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b. Read issue body and comments only through 6181243726; no sibling posts. Static source verification, not executed fixtures or live-host coverage.

Existing mechanisms: paths.ts already recursively collects named path fields through arguments/tool_input/toolInput/input/params, deduplicates targets, and unions ApplyPatch body paths. tools.ts already admits proxy names and the #3593 write-name grammar. dispatcher.ts already denies ApplyPatch with empty/unclassified body harvest, admits target sets against effective worktree roots, and composes project/story fences. Reuse these mechanisms.

### F1 — blocks-the-design — P3: name-only unwrap does not unwrap shell input
Evidence: [effectiveHookToolName and innerMcpToolName](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b/packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts) return a name only. [hookShellCommand](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b/packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts) reads command/cmd from the first tool-input record or top level, not tool_input.arguments.command. The existing shell dispatcher also runs before effectiveName is computed.

Failure: use_tool with tool_input={tool_name:"Bash",arguments:{command:"git push",path:"src/a.ts"}} has a harvested path, but merely changing the name predicates still yields no command for Shell/UAT. An untrusted extra path also defeats an empty-harvest-only shell fallback.

Consequence: amend limb 3 to route a consistent effective name AND effective argument view through the existing shell pipeline, including UAT and destructive-command checks. Preserve payload-root identity for grants and worktree attribution. Require wrapped/unwrapped command parity fixtures, including a decoy path. This is wrapper extraction, not expansion of #4199 shell-command grammar.

### F2 — blocks-the-design — P1/P4: URI strings are not filesystem destinations
Evidence: collectPathishFields passes strings unchanged; [dispatcher.toProjectRelativePosix](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts) uses path.resolve/relative, with no URI decoding.

Failure: adding uri to PATHISH_KEYS makes file:///repo/secret.txt nonempty, but lexical path resolution checks a synthetic file:/... path instead of /repo/secret.txt. A denylist-only fence can therefore miss the real target; unsupported schemes likewise become apparent local paths.

Consequence: specify supported local file-URI decoding before root admission and fence evaluation, with explicit refusal of unsupported or malformed destinations in the applicable write gate. Test percent escapes, Windows drive/authority cases, and mixed valid/invalid targets; one valid target must not conceal an unresolved destination. Do not equate nonempty harvest with complete classification.

### F3 — sharpens-framing — P2/P3: distinguish unknown writes from ordinary shell commands
Evidence: the current dispatcher intentionally routes shell commands through operation classifiers and allows unclassifiable nonmutating commands such as git status. The draft's limb 2 also covers every shell-shaped proxy with empty destination harvest.

Failure: a wrapped git status normally has no path field, so a literal universal empty-harvest deny blocks it even though its direct spelling remains allowed.

Consequence: state whether this asymmetry is intentional. Prefer effective shell classification first, preserving recognized read-only behavior and denying unresolved mutation under the applicable authority policy. Keep unconditional unknown-destination denial for write-shaped calls explicit. If all wrapped shell without a destination is deliberately forbidden, record that compatibility cost and test it rather than claiming transparent reclassification.

### F4 — sharpens-framing — P4: keep the null-path fix at the active-fence boundary
Evidence: dispatcher already returns early when fenceActive is false, then passes [null to evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b/packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts), whose null branch allows when edits are enabled. The dispatcher conversion itself returns string, not null.

Failure: an empty target set under an active denylist/story fence reaches that permissive branch. Describing this only as failed path conversion obscures the actual trigger.

Consequence: make the dispatcher active-fence/null-target deny explicit, with project-only and story-only fence tests and an inactive-fence control. That fits the declared file_scope without silently widening the shared policy evaluator's contract.

### F5 — footnote — protocol/recording
The deposit matches the inclusive ceiling and names three claimed families; it does not prove panel completion. Stop 1 includes a refutation-target despite the open-critique charter; I treated it as thread data, not a restriction on this audit. Parent should preserve open critique in subsequent envelopes and own the sibling census, successor disposition map, and Dual-stop/pain audit. No implementation or repository edits were performed.

## Pin verification (dispatch-sha 97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b)

Method: `git show 97ca8ce33f54cacf87733a156ab6ad7430cbca5b:<path>` for paths.ts, tools.ts, dispatcher.ts, and evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite in runtime-authority.ts. Prefer-A draft 6181223893 + Stop 1 6181224099 + panel-deposit 6181243726 only (input-ceiling inclusive). No sibling Round-1 reads.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

- PATHISH_KEYS / collectPathishFields / hookMutationTargetPaths (paths.ts): harvests file_path|filePath|path|target_file|targetFile|target_path|targetPath (+ nested arguments/tool_input/input/params). Omits uri and file.
- #3593 MCP write-shaped admission: isMcpWriteShaped + isMcpProxyWrapper + effectiveHookToolName unwrap; MCP_HOOK_MATCHER selects CallMcpTool|use_tool.
- ApplyPatch empty-harvest / unclassified-body deny: applyPatchBodyUnclassified; inspectMutationGates denies ApplyPatch when mutationTargets.length===0 or applyPatchHarvestedInputUnclassified; runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite also denies applyPatchBodyUnclassified under an active fence. Precedent Prefer-A limb 2 matches.
- Shell/UAT slice: decideHook gates on outer isShellTool(toolName) before the MCP branch.
- Write fence: resolveWriteFence + evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite; documented null-path pass at library layer.

## Pain audit vs Prefer-A draft 6181223893

### pain-P1 — CONFIRMED; Prefer-A limb 1 addresses
Evidence: PATHISH_KEYS at pin has no uri/file. MCP dests only in those fields → collectPathishFields / hookMutationTargetPaths empty.
Failure mode: write-shaped MCP with dest in uri/file never enters inspectMutationGates via the length>0 conjunct.
Disposition: limb 1 (add uri/file, keep existing keys) is necessary; harvest-only without limb 2 is in Prefer-A Reject and remains rejected here.

### pain-P2 — CONFIRMED; Prefer-A limb 2 addresses
Evidence: decideHook MCP branch requires `isMcpWriteShaped(effectiveName) && !isShellTool(toolName) && !isSpawnTool(toolName) && hookMutationTargetPaths(...).length > 0` before inspectMutationGates. Empty harvest skips the gate; outer use_tool/CallMcpTool is not isDirectWriteTool → not-direct-write allow.
Failure mode: write-shaped effective name + empty dest harvest fail-opens under active UAT/fence.
Disposition: limb 2 fail-closed on write-shaped (or proxy with write-/shell-shaped inner) + empty harvest, matching ApplyPatch unclassified-body deny, closes the skip.

### pain-P3 — CONFIRMED; Prefer-A limbs 2–3 address
Evidence: Shell routing uses outer `isShellTool(toolName)`. MCP branch computes effectiveName but still gates `!isShellTool(toolName)` on the outer name. isMcpWriteShaped("run_terminal_command") is false (no write markers; falls through to false). Inner Grok shell via use_tool never hits Shell/UAT; falls through to not-direct-write allow.
Failure mode: proxy-wrapped run_terminal_command/monitor/Bash skips Shell classifier and UAT shell path.
Disposition: after unwrap, re-run isShellTool(effectiveName) / isDirectWriteTool(effectiveName) / isMcpWriteShaped so inner shell hits Shell/UAT (limb 3). See F1 for ordering vs limb 2.

### pain-P4 — CONFIRMED; Prefer-A limb 4 addresses
Evidence: runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite does `toCheck = targets.length > 0 ? targets : [null]` under fenceActive. evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite: when relPathPosix is null it returns allowed true, with comment that unclassifiable paths pass (host gap documented for Shell/MCP). dispatcher toProjectRelativePosix returns string (null only when target is null).
Failure mode: active write fence silently allows when dest cannot be classified.
Disposition: limb 4 deny under active fence when path cannot be classified. See F2 for file_scope vs library SoT.

## Findings

### F1 — sharpens-framing
Evidence: isMcpWriteShaped(run_terminal_command) is false; SHELL_TOOL_NAMES includes run_terminal_command/monitor; shell harvests command, not dest path.
Failure mode: applying limb-2 ApplyPatch-class empty-dest deny to shell-shaped proxy inners would mis-deny or still skip Shell/UAT.
Disposition consequence: Bound MUST sequence limb-3 unwrap then isShellTool(effectiveName) routing (and isDirectWriteTool) ahead of / disjoint from limb-2 write-shaped empty-harvest fail-closed. Empty-dest deny targets write-shaped effective names; shell-shaped inners go to Shell/UAT.

### F2 — sharpens-framing
Evidence: P4 silent-allow lives at (a) dispatcher toCheck:[null] under fenceActive and (b) runtime-authority.ts null→allow. Prefer-A file_scope lists paths.ts / tools.ts / dispatcher.ts / CHANGELOG — not runtime-authority.ts.
Failure mode: changing only the library without dispatcher, or only MCP empty-harvest without the fence null path, leaves a residual allow under fenceActive.
Disposition consequence: Prefer-A file_scope as drafted is fine if Bound names the dispatcher fenceActive + unclassifiable/null deny (the toCheck:[null] site) as the P4 limb. Widen file_scope to runtime-authority.ts only if Bound changes the library null-pass itself. Limb 2 alone does not close P4 for non-MCP direct-write empty targets that reach runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite.

### F3 — footnote
Evidence: uri/file values may be https:/mcp: schemes, not filesystem paths.
Failure mode: over-parsing URIs in this slice risks scope creep past #3593 keep-outs.
Disposition consequence: harvest uri/file as pathish strings; rely on existing relative/foreign/fence deny paths for non-fs values. Do not invent URI grammar here. Aligns with keep-out: do not rewrite #3593 admission grammar wholesale.

### F4 — footnote
Evidence: ApplyPatch empty-body deny already exists at inspectMutationGates and runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite; Prefer-A keep-outs say do not weaken it.
Failure mode: none if limb 2 mirrors rather than merges/weakens ApplyPatch.
Disposition consequence: Bound should add a parallel write-shaped-empty-harvest deny; leave ApplyPatch unclassified-body messages and predicates intact.

## Prefer-A limb stress (summary)

1. Harvest uri/file — necessary for P1; keep existing keys.
2. Empty-harvest fail-closed for write-shaped / write-shaped inners — necessary for P2; match ApplyPatch class; Reject harvest-only stands.
3. Unwrap then reclassify shell/direct-write/MCP-write — necessary for P3; order per F1.
4. No silent allow on relPathPosix null under active fence — necessary for P4; site per F2.
5. file_scope — adequate with F2 disposition; tools.ts may be tests-only if helpers already export what dispatcher needs.
6. Keep-outs — agree: no #3593 rewrite, no #4199 Shell-harvest absorb, no ApplyPatch weaken.
Reject list — agree; do not accept harvest-only, docs-only fail-open, or outer-name forever without unwrap reclassify.

## In plain English

At pin 97ca8ce, PreToolUse really does miss MCP dests sitting in uri/file, skip the write gates when harvest is empty for write-shaped MCP/proxy names, miss Shell/UAT for inner shell wrapped in use_tool/CallMcpTool, and allow under an active write fence when the relative path is null. Prefer-A draft 6181223893 hits all four pains. No design blockers. Two framing sharpens: (1) route shell-shaped proxy inners to Shell/UAT before applying write-shaped empty-dest deny; (2) put the P4 deny at the dispatcher fenceActive+null site unless file_scope widens to runtime-authority.ts. Footnotes only on URI schemes and preserving ApplyPatch deny. clean-result: yes.
